title: site.json
description: A content site's placement config: what the site-template assembler reads from `site/site.json` to write the deployable Next app. Every object is closed, so a misspelt key is an error rather than a silent no-op. Paths are relative to `site/` unless a key says otherwise.

$schema.description: Editor hint only; the assembler ignores it.

output.description: The app directory the assembler writes, relative to the site repo's root, e.g. `websites/main`: under `websites/`, at least two segments, none of them `.`, `..` or empty, and not under `websites/external`, which holds the site's submodules. Its parent is the pnpm workspace root.

port.description: The local dev server's port: `next dev -p <port>`, and the origin `frameSiteUrl` falls back to.

siteUrl.description: The site's public origin, e.g. `https://example.com`: the canonical, Open Graph, sitemap and robots URLs are built on it. `frameSiteUrl` takes it after the `SITE_URL` env var and before Vercel's production hostname, so a project whose Vercel production domain is not the custom one still names the right host. Absent: the env, then Vercel, then `http://localhost:<port>`.

theme.description: A key of the template's `themes.json`: the theme stylesheet and the fonts it needs.

tokens.description: The site's token sheet, e.g. `theme.css`. Only custom-property declarations inside `:root { }`; it is appended after the theme and the frame sheets.

mark.description: The hero's mark. Absent: `/glyph.svg` (content-buildr's glyph) as a glyph.

themeColor.description: The mobile browser chrome's colour; track the theme's ground.

ogImage.description: The Open Graph image's public path. Absent: the mark's `src`. When it is the mark's `src`, the twitter card is `summary` (the image beside the text); otherwise `summary_large_image`.

ogImageSize.description: The Open Graph image's size in pixels, given to unfurlers so they can lay out the card before the image loads. Absent: no size is declared.

ogImageType.description: The Open Graph image's media type, e.g. `image/jpeg`, written as `og:image:type`. Absent: no type is declared.

authorUrl.description: The author's own page. Given, the metadata's author carries it as `url` and the head links it as `<link rel="author">`. Absent: the author is a name only.

jsonLd.description: Structured data, rendered as one `application/ld+json` script in the root layout.

robotsDisallow.description: Paths production's robots.txt keeps crawlers out of — sign-in, an app behind it. Every other tier disallows everything already.

slots.description: Custom components by the place in the frame each fills. The value is a file under `site/components/` and its export, `file.tsx#Name`. A `band:<id>` key must name a section of `src/landing.json`. `bitbag` replaces the frame's bitbag — a `'use client'` component rendering `SiteBitbag` with the site's voice.

bands.description: The bands that step out of the soft/dark alternation, by section id (each must name a section of `src/landing.json`): a tone of their own, or no seam. What a look leaves out keeps the alternation's.

heroShot.description: How the hero draws its {shot}: "bleed" (the default) runs it full width under the hero; "thumbnail" draws it small, as a link that opens the full capture in a new tab. A thumbnail needs exactly one {shot} in the hero, naming a capture.

drawer.description: Drawer rows after the section rows. Where a row goes is config; what it says is copy: `nav` names its label under the copy's `nav.extra` (site.md's `# nav`, `## extra`).

dependencies.description: Extra npm dependencies, name to version range. Naming a dependency the template already has is refused.

toolkitPackages.description: Extra toolkit packages, as directories under the toolkit's `packages/web/packages/` (e.g. `releases`, `features/bitbag`), linked into the app.

family.description: This site's id among the Agentic Developer Hub family's members. Set, `/` ends with the family band: a card for every other member, from the site's `family` copy (`src/content/family/family.json`, from adhcontent's shared `content/family/`). The id must name a member there, which the frame checks at build. Absent: no family band.

analytics.description: Mount Vercel Web Analytics and Speed Insights in the root layout, on production deploys only (`DEPLOYMENT_ENV=production`). The assembler adds `@vercel/analytics` and `@vercel/speed-insights` to the app's dependencies.

rewrites.description: Next rewrites, e.g. a same-origin `/api/:path*` proxied to a backend. A `destination` may name environment variables as `${NAME}` or `${NAME:-default}`, substituted when `next.config.ts` loads: the environment's value if set and non-empty, else the `envDefaults` entry, else the inline default; with none, the build fails naming the variable.

headers.description: Next response headers: each rule's `source` is a Next path pattern, e.g. `/(.*)` for every route, and its `headers` the `{ key, value }` pairs sent with it — e.g. a site's security headers. Values are literal; nothing is substituted.

redirects.description: Next redirects, in the order Next matches them: each `{ source, destination, permanent }` as Next takes it — e.g. an old path sent on to where it lives now. Literal; nothing is substituted.

publicEnv.description: Variables passed through to Next's `env`, so client code reads them inlined at build. Each resolves as a `rewrites` reference does (environment, then `envDefaults`). A bare `NAME` with no value anywhere fails the build, naming it; `${NAME:-}` is the optional form, left out when it has no value.

envDefaults.description: Fallbacks for variables the environment leaves unset or empty, by name: a string (which may itself use `${…}`), or `{ by, values, local? }` — the value `values[<by>]` names, with `local` for a build off Vercel whose `by` names none (on Vercel that fails the build). `local` may itself be a `{ by, values, local? }` choice, one level deep, whose own `local` is a string: a backend picked by tier on Vercel and by build mode (`NODE_ENV`) off it.

fonts.description: Fonts beyond the theme's: one `next/font/local` family each, exposed as its CSS variable on `<html>`.

role.description: The theme custom property (or properties) this font fills, e.g. `--font-display`: `app/theme.css` gets `:root { <role>: var(<variable>), <fallback>; }`, one declaration per role. next/font hashes the family name, so this is how a theme's role reaches the self-hosted face.

fallback.description: The font stack after the face in its `role`, e.g. `ui-sans-serif, sans-serif`. Only used with `role`.

path.description: A font file under `site/`: woff2, woff, ttf or otf — the formats `next/font/local` serves.

preload.description: false: the face is not preloaded — the browser fetches it when a page paints in it. For a face the first screen does not set (an italic only the copy's emphasis reaches). It stays in the family. At least one face of a family must preload.
